title: Bidirectional A* in San Francisco: Route in ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* split the search: one wave grows from start, the other from goal, then they meet to reduce work. This is the same kind of speed trick behind autonomous vehicle routing and fast GPS-like navigation.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm ⚡ How autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds—by searching from both ends.

In this visualization (San Francisco, SoMa), the start-frontier and goal-frontier expand toward each other using heuristics, usually like A* but run bidirectionally. When the two searches meet, you stitch the best partial paths into the final route—often faster than one-way A* because you cut the explored area.

Takeaway: If your heuristic is informative, bidirectional search can drastically reduce the number of nodes expanded.

Debate question: Would you rather optimize for the fastest first answer, or the fewest expansions (best for battery + compute)?
